tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'duo_pose' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'pose': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'duo_hinge' reports the pose, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the pose and angle with 'duo_hinge'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'duo_pose' and take a 'screenshot'; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

pose.description: For 'duo_pose': the pose to move the hinge to.

angle.description: For 'duo_pose' with pose 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

JusPrin 2 is a major upgrade. We rebuilt nearly everything: it is now built on OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and every project has AI working beside it. The goal is the one JusPrin started with: make 3D printing simpler for hobbyists. You tell AI what you are printing and what went wrong. AI reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again.

## What AI can do

Each project has an AI chat beside the 3D view. Ask in plain words, and AI works in the open project:

- Set up the printer, filament and print settings for the part you are printing.
- Open a model or project file, place objects on the plate, and lay out plates.
- Cut, split, merge and repair objects.
- Change print settings for you.
- Slice the plate and check the result, for example support printed inside a hole, or a part that starts in the air.
- Look at a photo of a failed print and suggest what to change.
- Run a filament calibration test (temperature, flow or pressure advance), read a photo of the printed test, and save the result as a new filament preset.

When you ask AI to print, it opens the usual send dialog. You choose the options and press Send. AI never starts a print.

When a slice has a problem, a marker on the 3D view shows it. Press Ask AI to have AI explain the problem and your options.

## Ways to use AI

- Sign up for a JusPrin account in the app. New accounts get free credits, and no card is needed.
- Use your own OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter API key.
- Connect an AI app you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cowork, Cursor or VS Code. It can then work with the project open in JusPrin.
- Or skip AI and just slice.

## Also new

- **Home screen.** Your projects and printers are on one screen. Each printer card shows the printer's status, and once the printer is connected, opens its own window.
- **Printers.** Add a printer and connect it by chatting with AI. You can connect Bambu Lab printers in LAN mode, and Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint printers.
- **Saving.** Projects save themselves, so JusPrin never asks you to save or discard. File › Save (Cmd+S on a Mac, Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) keeps a version you can go back to in File › Version history. Saving doesn't write over the .3mf file you opened. To get a .3mf file, use File › Export › Project 3MF (Cmd+Shift+S or Ctrl+Shift+S).
- **Opening files.** A file you open from Finder or File Explorer opens as a new project. A model dropped on the 3D view is added to the open project.
- **Check print.** Print › Check print shows a report of the slice beside the preview.
- **Print history.** Every sliced file you export or send to a printer is listed on Home's Print history, and you can print it again from there.
- **Classic view.** View › Switch to classic view shows OrcaSlicer's full interface. Press Back to JusPrin to return.
- **Updates.** JusPrin checks its GitHub releases for a new version once a day. You see the result in Preferences › Updates.
- **Reporting a problem.** Help › Report a problem opens a new GitHub issue in your browser, with the app's version and your system filled in.

## Upgrading from JusPrin 1.4

- **Installing.** On Windows, the installer replaces JusPrin 1. On a Mac, JusPrin 2 is also called JusPrin.app, so dragging it to Applications replaces JusPrin 1. On Linux, the AppImage is a new file, and JusPrin 1's AppImage stays where it is.
- **Your printers.** The first time JusPrin 2 starts, it offers to import your printers from JusPrin 1 or OrcaSlicer, with their filaments and print settings. You choose which printers to import. You can import later with Printer › Import printers from JusPrin 1 or Import printers from OrcaSlicer.
- **Your JusPrin 1 folder.** JusPrin 2 keeps its settings in a new folder. It only reads JusPrin 1's folder and never changes it. JusPrin 1's app settings, such as units and language, aren't imported.
- **Your account.** Your JusPrin 1 sign-in doesn't carry over. To use AI with a JusPrin account, sign up in JusPrin 2, even if you had an account in JusPrin 1. Chats from JusPrin 1 aren't imported.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

When every step passes for every page, the command writes the app's version to that file. A run with `--skip-app`, with `--area`, or without `--ask-ai` leaves it as it was. 36-- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it. every page passes, it writes the app's version (Updates/Version.hpp) to

import os

import subprocess

    print(f"\n== {title}\n   {' '.join(map(str, command))}", flush=True)

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Checks the app guide and rebuilds what is built from it.")
    parser.add_argument("--area", help="one page, by its file name without .md")
    parser.add_argument("--skip-app", action="store_true", help="do not run the app: no walk, no new pictures")

    results = {}

            "1/3 walking the pages in the app and taking their pictures",

content.content:
=== 3c134d39e3 Report every failure a person cannot act on; keep a sentence only where they can
An error is expected only when the person can do something about it and
Kenneth decided what they are told. Every other failure now stops the work,
travels up unchanged and is reported once, by the handler at the top of its
entry point, and the person reads "Something went wrong on our side".
Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing
about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to
report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as
much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause
analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

Top handlers
- reported(doing, body), in Support/ErrorReport.hpp, wraps every CallAfter
  body, timer, HTTP callback and thread JusPrin's own code starts. Before,
  an exception from a CallAfter or a timer ended the main loop, and one from
  an HTTP callback or a thread called std::terminate: a model list entry
  without "id" aborted the app at launch (exit 134).
- report_unexpected_error moves itself to the main thread when called from
  another. A failure the person already answered in this run is not asked
  about again, so its dialog cannot reopen itself; automatic reports, which
  open no dialog, still send each one.
- An exception leaving any other native event stays OrcaSlicer's, as
  Kenneth decided; GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop is unchanged.

AI requests
- A failed request names its cause only where the person can act. On a
  JusPrin account, by the gateway's error code: signed out, out of credits,
  app too old, request too large, too many requests. With their own key, by
  the HTTP status alone: 401, 413, 429. No answer at all says the service
  could not be reached.
- Every other answer, an error the service sends inside a reply, and a reply
  cut short or unreadable throw UnexpectedServiceAnswer with the service's
  status, request id and body. The sentences for an overloaded, unavailable,
  timed-out, paused or cut-short service are deleted, and
  StreamEvent::Kind::Incomplete with them. The model declining to answer
  (stop reason "refusal") keeps its sentence: it is the model's answer, not
  a failure.
- A tool call that fails in the app's own work still goes to the AI model,
  and is also reported when automatic reports are on, with no dialog. A file
  the person picked that OrcaSlicer will not read answers "refused" and is
  not reported. When the saved projects cannot be read, the call's message
  carries the file system's reason.
- An AI service set up in another window during a reply is installed once
  the reply ends, instead of being dropped.

Account, sign-in and settings
- An account, account box, model list or sign-in answer that is the
  server's fault (a 5xx, or an answer the app cannot read) is reported. No
  answer and a 4xx refusal keep their sentences.
- A key or a sign-in the settings file could not keep throws. The "works
  until restart" warning and its row are gone.
- Delete account waits while a printer or filament chat replies, as it
  already did for the project chat.
- "Sign in" runs the web view's own address check, as "Sign up free" does.
  An address that check passes and the server refuses now reads
  "“alex@gmail” is not a complete email address. Check it, then try again."
  with the address the person typed. The password path is unchanged.

Chats, attachments and saves
- A chat checkpoint, chat switch, restoration or new chat whose save fails
  throws the autosave's own error instead of a sentence made up for it.
  Attachment blobs, attachment folders, the chat-titles file and a stored
  chat state that cannot be read or written throw with the file system's
  error. The timer's own checkpoint leaves alone the one failure the
  autosave has just recorded and already shows as "Couldn't save".
- A message or action a newer build wrote is kept as written and not shown,
  instead of being read as another kind.
- A file dropped on Home is copied with write_file (Support/Files: write,
  then rename), so a write the file system cuts short is an error and not a
  shorter file.

Home and Print history
- A print report answer nobody decided is reported. A refused report shows
  the next step: an ended sign-in shows the chat's sentence for it, an
  unreadable photo "That photo could not be read."
- A photo over 20 MB is refused when it is chosen: "That photo is larger
  than 20 MB. Choose a smaller photo, then send the report again."
- While the projects folder cannot be read, Print history shows Home's
  sentence, "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying.",
  keeps no history, and lists again by itself once the folder can be read.
- An exported G-code file is "not found" only when its path is not there;
  any other failure to read it is reported.
- A printer window whose secure connection cannot be checked says "The
  printer at %s answered, but JusPrin couldn't check its secure connection.
  If the printer's address starts with https://, change it to http:// in
  Printer settings, then try again." Checked on macOS only: on Windows and
  Linux an https address on a printer that only speaks http probably still
  says "Nothing answered".

Start report
- When the server answers the app's start report with a fault, the app
  reports it through report_if_automatic: sent only when automatic reports
  are on, and no dialog opens. When nothing answers (no network, a refused
  connection, a timeout) nothing is reported. Before, both cases only wrote
  a log line. report_if_automatic now moves itself to the main thread, as
  report_unexpected_error does. Kenneth, 2026-11-16, quoting the proposal
  back: "My proposal, not built: no dialog, and a report only when the
  server answers with a fault and the person has automatic reports on.
  Having no network at start stays silent. - go with your proposal".

Kenneth accepted the three new sentences (photo too large, incomplete
address, secure connection) on 2026-11-16: "Yes, all three". They and "That
photo could not be read." are in the catalogs, AI translated in all 22
languages.

Shell harness: new modes --delete-account-waits and --printer-window; the
dialog closer answers only the innermost modal dialog; the stand-in server
answers the account box with 204, as the server does; checks count the app
log's "Unexpected error while" lines where a folder cannot be read or
written; print_history_stopped_print_has_no_row replaces a check that
expected a "Started" row removed on 2026-11-08; the detach check installs an
agent the profile does not pick with --fake-printer too.

=== fbf378bc94 Shell harness: open the printer chat through the shell, as the app does
Several shell harness modes (--printer-setup, --printer-chat-sheet,
--print-host-check, --printer-network-check, --printer-connect-skill)
called PrinterPanel::open directly. That shows the panel but skips the
shell, which in the app hides Home and the project tabs and gives the
chat the whole window. So the harness window showed Home squeezed into
the left half with the chat beside it, a layout no person ever sees.
The real app was checked by opening the printer chat three ways; each
time the chat covered the whole window.

A new helper, open_printer_chat, opens the chat through
ShellController::open_printer_conversation, the path Home and the header
use. The shell opens no chat while one is open, so the helper first
closes an open chat and waits until its close (which finishes on a later
event turn) is done. It then checks that the chat is shown and that Home
is hidden.

Tested on macOS:
- --printer-setup: 348 checks pass, 0 fail. With the old direct opening
  put back, 6 of the new "chat covers Home" checks fail.
- --print-host-check and --printer-chat-sheet: pass.
- --printer-connect-skill: the new checks pass; 3 other checks
  (skill_add_settled, connect_skill_printer_added,
  connect_skill_comes_with_printer_add) fail, the same 3 that fail on
  the unchanged harness.
- --printer-network-check: not run, it needs Bambu's real plug-in.

=== 70f08918d8 Fix two agent tests that failed only on Windows
Two cases in agent_bridge_tests failed on Windows and passed on macOS.
Both mistakes were in the tests; the app code they check was right.

"pick_attachment opens the dialog for one kind and stages the chosen
files" wrote its sample G-code file in text mode. On Windows text mode
writes "\n" as "\r\n", so the app's preview of the file was "G1 X0\r\n"
and the check for "G1 X0\n" failed. The test now writes the file in
binary mode.

"the account comes with the titles of the chats it charged" kept its own
std::ifstream on chat-titles.json open until the end of the test, and the
last line deletes the temp folder. Windows refuses to delete an open
file, so remove_all threw. The test now closes the file as soon as it
has parsed it.

Tested: agent_bridge_tests passes in full on Windows (579 cases, on the
GCP test VM) and on macOS (581 cases), and each of the two cases passes
when run alone on Windows.

=== f88b40865c Connect every print host type from the printer chat, not only Moonraker and OctoPrint
GitHub issue TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#40: an Elegoo Centauri Carbon
could not be connected from its printer chat. Its profile saves it with the
Elegoo Link connection type, and the chat refused every type except
Moonraker and OctoPrint. The AI asked to connect it as Moonraker, and the
app refused before sending any request to the printer.
Nothing in the history or earlier sessions gave a reason for the limit.
Kenneth, asked whether to open it to Elegoo Link only or to every type: "To every type."

printer_host_connect now takes every connection type OrcaSlicer's printer
settings offer except the three online services the person signs in to
(Obico, SimplyPrint, 3DPrinterOS), which need that sign-in, not an address.
Moonraker and OctoPrint keep their own tests. Every other type runs
OrcaSlicer's own test for it, the one its Physical Printer dialog's Test
button runs, unchanged. Those requests have no time limit, so the test runs
on a thread of its own and the chat gives up after the same 30 seconds as
the other tests; the thread is left to finish, and against a host that
never answers it holds one socket until the app quits. A refused test
(HTTP 401 or 403) opens the API key form, as it does for Moonraker and
OctoPrint.

A printer with no saved address is no longer reported as "unavailable" for
the type its profile defaults to, since the person never chose that type:
a Neptune 4 or Creality K1 can be connected as Moonraker. The connection
skill now says the saved type is the starting point, explains Elegoo Link
model by model from the app's code (Centauri Carbon: its web page names
ELEGOO, no key; Centauri Carbon 2: an access code, 123456 by default, typed
in the form labelled "API key"), and names the types the chat cannot finish
(Repetier, UltiMaker, PrusaLink with a user name and password) and where
the person can. The issue report's footer names the type tried and, when
different, the type the printer is saved with. The guide's sentence on
which printers connect is updated.

Tested: agent_bridge_tests (583 cases) and the AgentUI page tests (833)
pass. The new C++ tests check the types the tool takes, an Elegoo Link
printer through connecting and the key form, and the footer; the two new
skill tests fail on the old skill text. In the real app on macOS, against
stand-in hosts on this Mac: a Centauri Carbon connected from the chat and
Home showed "Connected · Elegoo Link"; a Centauri Carbon 2 was refused with
no code, the key form opened, and the typed code connected; a Prusa MK4 at
a host that never answers reported no answer within 30 seconds; a Neptune 4
whose person said they use Mainsail connected as Moonraker to a Moonraker

content.content:
=== d010a88c1a Read printer sizes the same in every language
When JusPrin runs in a language that writes decimals with a comma
(Portuguese, German, French, Spanish, Russian and others), the add-printer
form showed no nozzle sizes for almost every printer, so the printer could
not be added. GitHub issue TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#39 reports it for
the Flashforge Creator 5 Pro and its 0.4 mm nozzle.

wxWidgets sets the C library's number format to the app's language at
startup. JusPrin's printer catalog read the sizes in the printer profiles
with std::stod, which follows that format, so "0.4" read as 0. With the
number format set to Portuguese, 412 of 454 printer models lost their
nozzle sizes, and fractional bed sizes were cut short (233.5 mm read as
233). The same mistake read a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF as 0, and
told the AI about a nozzle mismatch as "0,2" instead of "0.2".

On macOS the bug is usually hidden: an app opened from Finder has no LANG
setting, and the bundled Python's startup then resets the whole C locale
to "C". Python does this only on Unix, so Windows always shows the bug.

The catalog, the printer backend and the 3MF facts now parse with
OrcaSlicer's locale-independent string_to_double_decimal_point and
atof_decimal_point. The mismatch text is written by the JSON library
instead of snprintf. The test programs compile LocalesUtils.cpp directly,
as they do the JusPrin sources they test.

Tested: three new tests switch the number format to Portuguese; each fails
without this change and passes with it. jusprin_tests (180 cases) and
agent_bridge_tests (581 cases) pass, and the clang-tidy include check
passes on the changed lines. In the real app on macOS, started with LANG
set and the language set to Portuguese, JusPrin 2.0.0 showed no nozzle
size for the Creator 5 Pro and kept Continue disabled; this build showed
0.25, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm and added the printer with its 0.4 mm profile.
Not run on Windows.

=== b3eed3bf4b Report unexpected errors to the JusPrin team, and fix four bugs found on the way
When something fails that no person can act on, JusPrin now shows one
dialog, "Something went wrong on our side" (boards agent-ui-11 to 16),
instead of a sentence about that particular failure. The person can see
the whole report, press "Report to JusPrin team", or tick "From now on,
report errors like this automatically". The report goes to JusPrin's
server (/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports), which passes it to Sentry.

Why: under the error-handling rules, a failure with no outcome a person
decided travels up unchanged to the top of its entry point and is
reported there, instead of each site writing its own sentence. Kenneth
agreed to this on 2026-11-15: "Yes, go with this approach."

The reporting path
- Support/ErrorReport: report_unexpected_error() logs the error, then
  sends it at once when automatic reports are on, or queues it for the
  dialog after the current event. A failure that repeats while its dialog
  waits is queued once; after the person answers, the next occurrence
  opens the dialog again, and every occurrence is sent when reports are
  automatic (Kenneth: "leave it"). A report holds the app and OS versions,
  what the app was doing, the error and, for page errors, the stack. The
  home folder becomes "~", a file-system error's paths become "<path>",
  and each field is cut to the server's limit. The send is anonymous: no
  token or cookie.
- Shell/ErrorReportDialog: the dialog, drawn with the design tokens. Its
  line "no chat messages, no files, no project names and no account or
  email address" stays although other error text can quote a file name
  (Kenneth: "Keep the promise and accept the risk.").
- Top handlers: the AI pages' and Home's message handlers, the file
  picker's callback (it reads the chosen files after the page's message
  was handled), and both pages' own top level (window "error" and
  "unhandledrejection", sent as a new report_error message and queued
  until the page has connected).
- An exception that leaves any other native event is handled exactly as
  OrcaSlicer handles it; no OrcaSlicer-owned file is changed. Kenneth: "it
  should behave the same as the upstream. no reason to use a diff
  behavior here for the fork".
- Preferences › Updates: a new "Error reports" box, "Report errors to the
  JusPrin team automatically", off by default.

Five failures now take that path, with their sentences removed:
- "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again." (the AI page and Home)
- "The file could not be read." (an attachment that is not base64, or a
  chosen or dropped file that cannot be opened or read)
- "The G-code couldn't be written to %s." (exporting from print history)
=== 00953649de Translate JusPrin into upstream OrcaSlicer's 22 languages
JusPrin's own windows and its AI and Home pages showed English in every
language. Every string a person reads in them is now marked and translated
into the 22 languages upstream ships, in catalogs of the fork's own so that
taking an upstream release never conflicts in one:

- Localization/native/<lang>.po for native text, collected by
  Localization/update_catalogs.py (text upstream's template already has
  keeps upstream's translation) and merged by Brand/brand_catalogs.py into
  the catalog the app loads.
- Localization/pages/<lang>.po for both pages, through Lingui 5.9.5. The app
  passes its language as ?lang=; the page activates it before any module
  runs.

Text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool results), logs, error reports,
identifiers and names stay English. The translations are machine-made and
marked "# AI Translated"; entries a translator was unsure of also carry
"# Needs human review: <what to check>". Terms follow upstream's catalog
and the OrcaSlicer localization glossary.

Sentences that were built from translated pieces are now one message each,
with placeholders and plural forms, and render the same English. Other
changes the translation needed:

- Support/Translate.hpp: GUI-free code marks text with L() and translates it
  with translated() and translated_plural(), which the app installs.
- "Model" and "Search models" in the printer picker, and "Plate" in the
  add-printer form, have contexts of their own, apart from the AI model and
  the project plate.
- Numbers JusPrin shows use the app language's separators
  (Support/DecimalText on the native side, decimalText on the pages): a
  German app reads "Kobra 3 · 0,4 mm".
- An untitled chat is titled with the translated "New chat"; the saved
  document keeps its English default.
- "Ask current chat about this" drafts its message in the app's language.
- The setup card's estimate row wraps its link to the next line when a
  translation is too long to share the row.
- All settings shows OrcaSlicer's setting labels, groups and values through
  OrcaSlicer's own catalog.
- Translator notes sit on the line of the string they describe, so xgettext
  gives each note to the right string.
- update_catalogs.py starts a new language with its own number of plural
  forms; Home type-checks Lingui from its own packages.

Server text the app shows follows the app's language: the account, account
=== 1c1007fe3b Error handling rules: a sentence of its own only where the person can act
Replaces the "Error handling discipline" list in AGENTS.md.

An error is expected only when the person can do something about it and
Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is
unexpected: no code where it happens, it travels up unchanged, and the one
handler at the top of the entry point reports it with everything known and
tells the person "Something went wrong on our side".

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing
about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to
report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as
much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause
analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

The rules name the error-handling skill, which is not in this commit.

decided travels up unchanged to the top of its entry point and is
reported there, instead of each site writing its own sentence. Kenneth
agreed to this on 2026-11-15: "Yes, go with this approach."

The reporting path
- Support/ErrorReport: report_unexpected_error() logs the error, then
  sends it at once when automatic reports are on, or queues it for the
  dialog after the current event. A failure that repeats while its dialog
  waits is queued once; after the person answers, the next occurrence
  opens the dialog again, and every occurrence is sent when reports are
  automatic (Kenneth: "leave it"). A report holds the app and OS versions,
  what the app was doing, the error and, for page errors, the stack. The
  home folder becomes "~", a file-system error's paths become "<path>",
  and each field is cut to the server's limit. The send is anonymous: no
  token or cookie.
- Shell/ErrorReportDialog: the dialog, drawn with the design tokens. Its
  line "no chat messages, no files, no project names and no account or
  email address" stays although other error text can quote a file name
  (Kenneth: "Keep the promise and accept the risk.").
- Top handlers: the AI pages' and Home's message handlers, the file
  picker's callback (it reads the chosen files after the page's message
  was handled), and both pages' own top level (window "error" and
  "unhandledrejection", sent as a new report_error message and queued
  until the page has connected).
- An exception that leaves any other native event is handled exactly as
  OrcaSlicer handles it; no OrcaSlicer-owned file is changed. Kenneth: "it
  should behave the same as the upstream. no reason to use a diff
  behavior here for the fork".
- Preferences › Updates: a new "Error reports" box, "Report errors to the
  JusPrin team automatically", off by default.

Five failures now take that path, with their sentences removed:
- "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again." (the AI page and Home)
- "The file could not be read." (an attachment that is not base64, or a
  chosen or dropped file that cannot be opened or read)
- "The G-code couldn't be written to %s." (exporting from print history)
=== 00953649de Translate JusPrin into upstream OrcaSlicer's 22 languages
JusPrin's own windows and its AI and Home pages showed English in every
language. Every string a person reads in them is now marked and translated
into the 22 languages upstream ships, in catalogs of the fork's own so that
taking an upstream release never conflicts in one:

- Localization/native/<lang>.po for native text, collected by
  Localization/update_catalogs.py (text upstream's template already has
  keeps upstream's translation) and merged by Brand/brand_catalogs.py into
  the catalog the app loads.
- Localization/pages/<lang>.po for both pages, through Lingui 5.9.5. The app
  passes its language as ?lang=; the page activates it before any module
  runs.

Text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool results), logs, error reports,
identifiers and names stay English. The translations are machine-made and
marked "# AI Translated"; entries a translator was unsure of also carry
"# Needs human review: <what to check>". Terms follow upstream's catalog
and the OrcaSlicer localization glossary.

Sentences that were built from translated pieces are now one message each,
with placeholders and plural forms, and render the same English. Other
changes the translation needed:

- Support/Translate.hpp: GUI-free code marks text with L() and translates it
  with translated() and translated_plural(), which the app installs.
- "Model" and "Search models" in the printer picker, and "Plate" in the
  add-printer form, have contexts of their own, apart from the AI model and
  the project plate.
- Numbers JusPrin shows use the app language's separators
  (Support/DecimalText on the native side, decimalText on the pages): a
  German app reads "Kobra 3 · 0,4 mm".
- An untitled chat is titled with the translated "New chat"; the saved
  document keeps its English default.
- "Ask current chat about this" drafts its message in the app's language.
- The setup card's estimate row wraps its link to the next line when a
  translation is too long to share the row.
- All settings shows OrcaSlicer's setting labels, groups and values through
  OrcaSlicer's own catalog.
- Translator notes sit on the line of the string they describe, so xgettext
  gives each note to the right string.
- update_catalogs.py starts a new language with its own number of plural
  forms; Home type-checks Lingui from its own packages.

Server text the app shows follows the app's language: the account, account
=== 1c1007fe3b Error handling rules: a sentence of its own only where the person can act
Replaces the "Error handling discipline" list in AGENTS.md.

An error is expected only when the person can do something about it and
Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is
unexpected: no code where it happens, it travels up unchanged, and the one
handler at the top of the entry point reports it with everything known and
tells the person "Something went wrong on our side".

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing
about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to
report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as
much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause
analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

The rules name the error-handling skill, which is not in this commit.

1	---
2	name: jusprin-worktree-build
3	description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: reference
7	  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
8	  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
9	---
10	
11	A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:
12	
13	```
14	cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
15	  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
16	  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
17	  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
18	  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
19	```
20	
21	ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).
22	
23	CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.
24	
25	The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
26	without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
27	RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
28	reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
29	[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].
30	
31	FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
32	does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
33	(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
34	them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
35	created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
36	shown; web-view crashes vanish).
37	
38	`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
39	not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
40	--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
41	/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.
42	
43	CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
44	repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
45	`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
46	worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
47	"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
48	`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
49	absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
50	stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

input.content:
JusPrin 2.0.1 speaks your language, connects more printers, and fixes adding a printer when the app is set to a language that writes decimals with a comma.

## New

- **Your language.** JusPrin's own windows, Home and the AI chat now follow the app's language, in the 22 languages OrcaSlicer ships. The translations are machine-made; if a sentence reads wrong, tell us with Help › Report a problem. AI still reads and writes in whatever language you chat in.
- **More printers connect from the printer chat.** Besides Bambu Lab, Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint, the chat now connects the other print hosts OrcaSlicer's printer settings offer, such as PrusaLink and Elegoo Link (Elegoo Centauri Carbon and Centauri Carbon 2).
- **Error reports.** When something goes wrong that you can't fix yourself, JusPrin says so in one window and lets you send us a report with one click. You can read the whole report before sending it. It holds no chat messages, files, project names, account or email address. To send these reports without being asked, tick **Report errors to the JusPrin team automatically** in Preferences › Updates.

## Fixed

- In Portuguese, German, French, Spanish, Russian and other languages that write decimals with a comma, the add-printer form showed no nozzle sizes for most printers, so the printer couldn't be added. Bed sizes such as 233.5 mm were also read short.
- A photo larger than 20 MB for a print report is now refused when you choose it, instead of failing when the report is sent.

## Also changed

- Each time JusPrin starts, it tells our server that it started, so we can count how many installs run. The message holds the app's version, the system's name and a random install number made on the first start. It holds nothing that names you. JusPrin doesn't send it when stealth mode is on.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

No, there's no release skill. Neither the project's skills folder (`.claude/skills/`) nor your global one (`~/.claude/skills/`) has one. I've been working from three written sources in the repo:

- The "Releasing" section of [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). It says the release workflow refuses a commit until it has three things: a version above every released one, a release notes file, and a guide check for that version.
- The top comment of [.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml](.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml), which says how to start the workflow. Its output is only a draft release, which you publish by hand.
- The "Before a release" section of [docs/guide/README.md](docs/guide/README.md), which explains the guide check.

There's also a memory note from the 2.0.0 release: no nightly or team testing round, test the draft's own files, then you publish.

**Done so far**, in a new worktree at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/release-2.0.1` on branch `claude/release-2.0.1`, cut from the tip of `jusprin-dev`:

- **Version:** set to 2.0.1 in [Version.hpp](.claude/worktrees/release-2.0.1/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp).
- **Release notes:** a draft is in [2.0.1.md](.claude/worktrees/release-2.0.1/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/2.0.1.md), built from the 13 commits since 2.0.0. It covers:
  - the app translated into 22 languages
  - more print hosts connecting from the printer chat, such as Elegoo Link and PrusaLink
  - the new error-report window and its automatic-reports setting
  - the fix for missing nozzle sizes in languages that write decimals with a comma
  - the 20 MB photo limit
  - a short note on the anonymous message the app now sends at each start

  Please read it; the wording is yours to change. I added the note about the start message because people should be told about it, but cutting it is up to you.
- **Build:** the guide check needs the test harness and web pages built from this commit. That build finished successfully.

**Still to do:**
1. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. While it runs, the app takes over the screen, so the computer needs to be left alone. With 8 guide pages it should take about 10 to 15 minutes. It writes `checked-version.txt` only if every page passes.
2. Check for screens that are new since 2.0.0 and that no guide page mentions. Then commit the version, the notes and the guide files.
3. With your yes: push to `jusprin-dev`, fast-forward `main`, and start the workflow with Mac signing turned on.
4. Test the draft's files, then you publish.
